problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}7 & 10 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

The triangle $S$ is mapped to the triangle ${S}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The triangle ${S}^{′}$ has vertices $(10,5),(0,-5),$ and $(15,20).$ Which of the following are vertices of $S?$

- $(9,5)$
- $(0,1)$
- $(10,-7)$

feedback.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The parallelogram $P$ is mapped to the parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The parallelogram ${P}^{′}$ has vertices $(-2,2),(-5,4),(-3,2),$ and $(0,0).$ Which of the following are vertices of $P?$

- $(-2,1)$
- $(0,0)$
- $(2,0)$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${P}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $P$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{3-2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of $P$ are $(0,2),(-1,2),(-1,0),(0,0).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
